question.problem:
Given that the log-likelihood function for a particular sample of independent exponential random variables is

$$
l(\theta )=5\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -15.8\text{ }\,\theta ,
$$

what is the maximum likelihood estimate $\overset{^}{\,\theta \,}$ from this sample? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
In order to find the maximum likelihood estimate of $\theta ,$ we calculate the derivative of the log-likelihood function, set the derivative equal to zero, and solve for $\theta .$

First, we take the derivative of $l(\theta ):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}l}{\text{d}\theta } & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }(5\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -15.8\text{ }\,\theta ) \\  & =\frac{5}{\theta }-15.8.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we set the derivative equal to $0$ and solve for $\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{\theta }-15.8 & =0 \\ \frac{5}{\theta } & =15.8 \\ 5 & =15.8\text{ }\,\theta  \\ \theta  & ≈0.316\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, for this sample, the maximum likelihood estimate of $\theta $ is $\overset{^}{\,\theta \,}≈0.316,$ rounded to $3$ decimal places.
